topic.angle: A region from which nothing escapes

card.title: A black hole is a place, not a thing

body.claim: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape.
body.why: In 1784 John Michell suggested that gravity near a massive, compact object could trap even light. Today a black hole is defined as a region from which no signal or object can escape. Sagittarius A*, at the centre of our Milky Way, holds one of about 4.3 million solar masses.

probes.question: Roughly how massive is the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way?
True or false: in 1784 John Michell proposed that gravity could be strong enough to trap even light.
